name: QUARTILE.EXC
description: QUARTILE.EXC returns the specified quartile (1st, 2nd, or 3rd) of a dataset using the exclusive method, which never returns the minimum or maximum values.
tldr: Returns quartile 1, 2, or 3 using the exclusive method (endpoints excluded).

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array of numeric values.

parameters.name: quart
parameters.description: Quartile to return: 1 (first), 2 (median), or 3 (third) only. Values 0 or 4 cause #NUM!.

basicExample.explanation: Exclusive rank = 0.5*(8+1) = 4.5; interpolate between the 4th (4) and 5th (5) values: 4.5.

advancedExamples.title: First quartile excludes endpoints
advancedExamples.description: Equivalent to PERCENTILE.EXC with k = 0.25, using rank k*(n+1).

advancedExamples.title: quart = 0 or 4 is invalid
advancedExamples.description: The exclusive method only supports quart 1, 2, and 3.
advancedExamples.explanation: quart = 0 requests the minimum, which the exclusive method cannot return.

howItWorks: QUARTILE.EXC uses the exclusive (EXC) method, internally equivalent to PERCENTILE.EXC(array, quart/4). It accepts only quart 1, 2, or 3 and computes a rank as k*(n+1) where k = quart/4. Because the method is exclusive, the result always lies strictly between the minimum and maximum, and quart 0 or 4 returns #NUM!. Values are interpolated when the rank is fractional. Text and logical values are ignored.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click where you want the quartile.

limitations: Only quart 1, 2, and 3 are valid; quart 0 or 4 cause #NUM!.
Interpolates, so results generally are not actual data values.

commonErrors.cause: quart is 0 or 4 (or outside 1..3), or the array is too small.
commonErrors.fix: Use quart 1, 2, or 3; for the min/max use QUARTILE.INC instead.
Choose .INC when endpoints are needed; .EXC otherwise.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports QUARTILE.EXC with the same exclusive behavior as Excel 2010+.

faq.question: What is the difference between .INC and .EXC?
faq.answer: .INC allows quart 0..4 (including the actual min and max) and uses rank 1 + k*(n-1). .EXC accepts only quart 1..3, uses rank k*(n+1), and never returns the endpoints.

faq.question: Why does QUARTILE.EXC(...,0) give #NUM!?
faq.answer: The exclusive method excludes the minimum, so quart 0 is invalid; use QUARTILE.INC for the minimum.

faq.question: When should I use QUARTILE.EXC?
faq.answer: When your definition requires the exclusive method (endpoints excluded), such as certain statistical textbook formulas.
